messages:
Priya (Support): Customer ACME reported streaming chat sessions only return the first SSE event then the connection drops. They say it works when they call our hosted API directly from their laptop, but fails when routed through their gRPC->HTTP gateway in prod. They attached a server log and a small Node repro.

Alex (SRE): Can you paste the minimal repro curl and a trimmed log snippet? Also which protocol did the gateway use HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 to talk to us?

Priya (Support): Repro from customer (they run a grpc-gateway that translates gRPC to HTTP/1.1 to our endpoint):

```
curl --http1.1 -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-mini"
```

Node snippet they used (simplified):

```
fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${t}` } })
  .then(res => {
    const reader = res.body.getReader();
    function pump(){
      return reader.read().then(({done, value}) => {
        if(done) return;
        process.stdout.write(new TextDecoder().decode(value));
        return pump();
      })
    }
    return pump();
  })
```

Priya (Support): Customer logs show 200 then FIN after ~8s. Our logs (when we proxied same request via their gateway) show the full stream was produced by runtime, including the trailing event. But the connection closed from the gateway side. Truncated trace: 

```
[redwood-runtime] 2026-01-22T14:12:01.123Z TX stream start id=0 client=...
[redwood-runtime] 2026-01-22T14:12:09.456Z EVENT send chunk bytes=2048
[redwood-runtime] 2026-01-22T14:12:12.789Z EVENT send chunk bytes=512
[redwood-runtime] 2026-01-22T14:12:15.000Z stream end id=0 status=200
```

```
[gateway-proxy] 2026-01-22T14:12:15.012Z upstream=closed by remote, code=FIN
[gateway-proxy] 2026-01-22T14:12:15.012Z proxied bytes truncated
```

Alex (SRE): Sounds like an intermediary (grpc-gateway/nginx/envoy) is buffering or deciding the response is done. Common pitfalls:
- HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 translation may try to set Content-Length when it shouldn't
- HTTP/1.1 intermediaries sometimes buffer until end or convert chunked -> non-chunked and close early
- Some gRPC->HTTP bridges don't handle `text/event-stream` flush semantics properly

Alex (SRE): Quick checklist to rule things out:
- Ask customer to try `curl --http2 -N` vs `--http1.1 -N` and compare (http2 sends frames, http1.1 uses chunked).
- Check whether gateway rewrites or strips `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` or sets `Content-Length` to 0/partial.
- Look for buffering flags (nginx: `proxy_buffering on/off`, envoy: `use_remote_address` isn't it but `stream_engine`? check `buffer` settings).

Maria (Eng-runtime): If the runtime is producing SSE properly (we saw the final `stream end`), then it's likely the gateway closed once it saw what it thought was end-of-body. Some gateways will convert HTTP/2 DATA frames to a buffered HTTP/1.1 response and set an incorrect Content-Length or EOF when idle timeouts/health checks hit.

Gabe: Also check auth renewal logic. If the gateway revalidates the token for each client chunk and the validation endpoint returns 401 mid-stream, some proxies will treat that as a failure and tear down the upstream. Customer said tokens are short lived.

Priya (Support): Customer looked and says their grpc-gateway runs with these settings by default; they tried toggling `proxy_buffering` but saw no change. They verified Authorization is sent once at start (not rechecked).

Alex (SRE): Can we ask them to capture raw headers on both sides? Specifically we want to see upstream->downstream headers that our runtime sent and what the gateway forwarded. Look for: `Transfer-Encoding`, `Content-Length`, `Connection`, `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `X-Accel-Buffering` (nginx), `grpc-status` or any grpc->http trailers.

Priya (Support): They sent a header dump. Gateway replaced `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` with `Content-Length: 1312` (incorrect), and then closed after 8s.

Maria (Eng-runtime): Bingo. If the gateway rewrites to a fixed Content-Length it will close the connection once it believes it’s sent expected bytes — and if the runtime flushes more events later (typical for SSE), those are dropped. For gRPC-gateway cases the bridge sometimes tries to aggregate.

Alex (SRE): Suggested fixes/workarounds we gave the customer:
1) Configure their grpc-gateway/nginx/envoy to not buffer SSE and to preserve `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `text/event-stream`. Example nginx directive: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection "";` and `proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;`.
2) If they can't change gateway, force client->our-api to use HTTP/1.1 chunked with `--http1.1 -N` or make a direct connection to hosted API bypassing their gateway.
3) Add a short server-side heartbeat event every 10s to keep intermediaries from timing out and to make some proxies treat stream as active. Example SSE heartbeat we recommended to runtime team: 

```
// server-side pseudo
setInterval(() => {
  res.write(':\n\n'); // comment line to flush
}, 10000);
```

Maria (Eng-runtime): Rolling a small compatibility enhancement in the runtime could help: an optional `sse-compat` header that causes the runtime to emit periodic `:\n\n` heartbeats and to ensure the first chunk flush includes no content-length. We should also log and emit a metric when we see `Connection: close` from upstream early. I'll open a short PR.

Gabe: Also called out that some gRPC gateways will inject `grpc-status` trailers which can confuse HTTP/1.1 bridges. If the gateway sees trailers, it may assume the stream is over. We should document known problematic gateways and recommended configs.

Priya (Support): Customer tried the heartbeat patch on their side (node) and saw the stream survive longer — events arrived as they were generated. They can't change the company-wide gateway config quickly though. They asked if we can do anything server-side.

Maria (Eng-runtime): We'll ship a small toggle in the API that customers can include as a header: `X-Redwood-SSE-Compat: 1`. When set, runtime will:
- emit a single initial flush chunk with a small prefix so intermediaries won't set a content-length,
- send heartbeats every 15s,
- avoid sending trailing HTTP/1.1 content-length header.
Agenda: PR in next sprint, canary behind a feature flag, document in support KB.

Alex (SRE): In the short term we asked customer to use the curl hack as a workaround and we provided a patch to their edge team config. They're testing now.

Support Bot: Reaction :thumbsup: — added customer ACME to "streaming-interop" watchlist.

Deploy Bot: Canary deployment queued for sse-compat flag on staging at 18:30 UTC.

Priya (Support): Follow-up: customer confirmed the workaround (heartbeat) + forcing unbuffered proxy fixed their immediate issue. They've reduced ticket priority but want the sse-compat header in product. We'll keep this thread for rollout notes and doc snippets.

Alex (SRE): Closing loop items:
- Maria to send PR + changelog blurb.
- Support to create KB: "Troubleshooting SSE through gRPC gateways" with sample nginx/envoy configs and curl tests.
- SRE to add metric alert if runtime observes upstream FIN before final event.

Maria (Eng-runtime): I'll post the PR link here once ready. Thanks everyone.

Gabe: FYI capture from packet trace shows the gateway indeed sent `FIN` immediately after the Content-Length bytes were forwarded. Attaching pcap to ticket.

Priya (Support): Thanks — updating customer and marking as "monitoring".
